title: Facebook Ads for Contractors: Guide + 58 Winning Ads

facts.fact: The vendor states Facebook (Meta) has over 3 billion monthly active users.
facts.quote: Facebook (Meta) has over 3 billion monthly active users, and the homeowners you want to reach are scrolling their feeds every single day.

facts.fact: The vendor states Google Ads for contractor keywords can cost $20-50+ per click.
facts.quote: Google Ads for contractor keywords can cost $20-50+ per click.

facts.fact: The vendor states pest control keywords hit $222 per click on Google.
facts.quote: Pest control keywords hit $222 per click on Google.

facts.fact: The vendor's realistic cost-per-lead benchmark for HVAC contractors on Facebook is $30–$75 per lead.
facts.quote: HVAC: $30–$75 per lead.

facts.fact: The vendor's realistic cost-per-lead benchmark for roofing contractors on Facebook is $50–$150 per lead.
facts.quote: Roofing: $50–$150 per lead.

facts.fact: The vendor states roofing job values are $8,000–$25,000+ per project.
facts.quote: the job values are higher ($8,000–$25,000+ per project)

facts.fact: The vendor's realistic cost-per-lead benchmark for landscaping contractors is $25–$60 per lead.
facts.quote: Landscaping: $25–$60 per lead.

facts.fact: The vendor's realistic cost-per-lead benchmark for plumbing contractors is $40–$80 per lead.
facts.quote: Plumbing: $40–$80 per lead.

facts.fact: The vendor's realistic cost-per-lead benchmark for pest control contractors on Facebook is $20–$50 per lead.
facts.quote: Pest Control: $20–$50 per lead.

facts.fact: The vendor's realistic cost-per-lead benchmark for electrical contractors is $35–$70 per lead.
facts.quote: Electrical: $35–$70 per lead.

facts.fact: The vendor's realistic cost-per-lead benchmark for pressure washing contractors is $15–$40 per lead.
facts.quote: Pressure Washing: $15–$40 per lead.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends starting a Meta lead generation campaign with a daily budget of $20–$50 per day.
facts.quote: Start with $20–$50 per day.

facts.fact: The vendor recommends a targeting radius of 15–30 miles around the contractor's base for most contractors.
facts.quote: 15–30 miles around your base is the sweet spot

facts.fact: The vendor recommends targeting homeowners aged 25–65+.
facts.quote: Target 25–65+.

facts.fact: The vendor states an ideal audience size in the service area is 100,000–500,000 people.
facts.quote: An audience of 100,000–500,000 in your service area is ideal.

facts.fact: The vendor states that closing one job from every 10–15 roofing leads is extremely profitable.
facts.quote: closing one job from every 10-15 leads is extremely profitable

facts.fact: The vendor's guide was published on March 26, 2026.
The article states that the odds of qualifying a lead are 21 times lower when a contractor calls at 30 minutes instead of 5 minutes (unattributed stat).
facts.quote: the odds of qualifying a lead are 21 times lower

facts.fact: The article claims retargeted website visitors who didn't request a quote convert at 3-5x the rate of cold audiences (unsourced claim by the vendor).
facts.unit: x conversion rate vs cold audiences
facts.quote: they convert at 3-5x the rate of cold audiences

facts.fact: The article says a lookalike audience can be built from a customer list of as few as 100 customers.
facts.quote: Upload your past customer list (even 100 customers works)

facts.fact: The article advises using no more than three to four form fields and claims each field added beyond that reduces conversion rate by 10-15% (unsourced).
facts.unit: % conversion rate drop per added field
facts.quote: Every field you add after that drops your conversion rate by 10-15%.

facts.fact: The article claims Meta's 'Higher Intent' lead form option reduces junk leads by 20-30% (unsourced).
facts.quote: This reduces junk leads by 20-30% while keeping your best prospects.

facts.fact: The article states Google Ads cost-per-click for pest control keywords averages $222.
facts.quote: With Google Ads CPC averaging $222 for pest control keywords

facts.fact: The article cites Facebook cost per lead for pest control of $20-50, which it calls 5-10x more cost-effective than Google Ads (unsourced).
facts.quote: Facebook’s $20-50 CPL is 5-10x more cost-effective.

facts.fact: The article gives an example HVAC offer of a $99 AC tune-up.
facts.quote: A $99 AC tune-up offer converts at a much higher rate

facts.fact: The article gives an example roofing financing offer of $0 down with payments as low as $149 per month on a $15,000 project.
facts.quote: “New roof, $0 down, payments as low as $149/month” makes a $15,000 project feel accessible.

facts.fact: The article gives an example plumbing lead magnet of $49 drain cleaning.
facts.quote: “$49 drain cleaning” or “Free water heater inspection” gets people in the door.

facts.fact: The article describes a WeatherTrigger rule example in which a roofer's storm response ad set switches on the day after wind gusts pass 60 km/h (product example from sister tool).
facts.quote: the storm response ad set switch on the day after wind gusts pass 60 km/h

facts.fact: The article gives a WeatherTrigger example in which a pressure washer cuts budget by half on days rain is forecast.
facts.unit: % budget cut on forecast rain days
facts.quote: A pressure washer can cut budget by half on days rain is forecast.

facts.fact: The article recommends responding to leads within 5 minutes and notes the ~21x qualification-odds gap versus a 30-minute callback.
facts.quote: when you call at 30 minutes instead of 5

facts.fact: The page's analysis sampled 58 contractor and home services lead ads from the public Meta Ad Library across roofing, HVAC, plumbing, pest control, lawn care, windows and solar.
facts.quote: We pulled 58 contractor and home services lead ads from the public Meta Ad Library across roofing, HVAC, plumbing, pest control, lawn care, windows and solar

facts.fact: Of the 58 sampled ads, 39 had been running for 90+ days.
facts.quote: 39 had been running for 90+ days, 18 for over a year, and the longest (an HVAC tune-up ad) for more than four years.

facts.fact: The longest-running sampled ad, an HVAC tune-up ad, had been running for more than four years.
facts.quote: the longest (an HVAC tune-up ad) for more than four years

facts.fact: The page's free Home Services Lead Ad Swipe Report contains 44 curated ads.
facts.quote: you can grab all 44 curated ads in the free

facts.fact: The page advises contractors to call leads within 5 minutes or they are wasting ad spend.
facts.quote: If you’re not calling leads within 5 minutes, you’re wasting ad spend.

facts.fact: The page recommends keeping ad audiences at 50,000+ people in the service area.
facts.quote: Keep audiences at 50,000+ in your service area.

facts.fact: The page states that a 5,000-person audience is too small for Facebook's algorithm to optimize.
facts.quote: A 5,000-person audience is too small for Facebook’s algorithm to optimize.

facts.fact: The page recommends testing 3-4 ad variations per campaign.
facts.quote: Always test 3-4 ad variations (different images, different headlines)

facts.fact: The page advises killing underperforming ads after 3-5 days.
facts.quote: Kill the underperformers after 3-5 days.

facts.fact: The page states Facebook's algorithm needs 50+ conversions per week to fully optimize.
facts.quote: Facebook’s algorithm needs 50+ conversions per week to fully optimize.

facts.fact: The page advises giving campaigns at least 7-14 days before judging performance.
facts.quote: Give campaigns at least 7-14 days before judging performance.

facts.fact: The page says a healthy lead-to-appointment rate is 20-40%, depending on trade.
facts.quote: A healthy rate is 20-40% depending on your trade.

facts.fact: The page claims most successful contractors see 5-15x return on ad spend from Facebook ads.
facts.quote: Most successful contractors see 5-15x ROAS on Facebook ads.

facts.fact: The page recommends a response-time goal of under 5 minutes during business hours.
facts.quote: Set a goal of under 5 minutes during business hours.

facts.fact: The page suggests a starting Facebook ad budget of $20-$50 per day, or $600-$1,500 per month.
facts.quote: Start with $20-$50 per day ($600-$1,500/month).

facts.fact: The page suggests scaling to $50-$150 per day once winning ads are identified.
facts.quote: Once you identify winning ads, scale to $50-$150/day.

facts.fact: The page says most successful contractor advertisers spend $1,000-$5,000 per month on Facebook ads.
facts.quote: Most successful contractor advertisers spend $1,000-$5,000/month on Facebook ads.

facts.fact: The page recommends keeping Lead Ads forms to 3-4 fields maximum.
facts.quote: keep the form to 3-4 fields maximum.

facts.fact: The page says leads can start appearing within 24-48 hours of launching a campaign.
facts.quote: You can start seeing leads within 24-48 hours of launching a campaign.

facts.fact: The page cites a $59 tune-up as an example of a priced entry offer used in contractor Facebook ads.
facts.quote: “$59 tune-up”, “$49 drain cleaning”, “free roof inspection”.
